questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How much sleep adults really need
Why yawns spread from person to person
How dogs learn to copy their owners
Why people get bored in meetings
questions.why: Georgina and Rob discuss why yawning is contagious and what research found.

questions.q: Why did Rob yawn at the start of the programme?
options: He was very tired
He was bored by the conversation
Georgina yawned first
He had just woken up
questions.why: Rob says he isn't tired or bored and yawned 'because you did'.

questions.q: Which animal does John Drury say may yawn when its owner yawns?
options: Dogs
Cats
Horses
Parrots
questions.why: He says, 'Dogs yawn when their owners yawn.'

questions.q: How does John Drury describe yawning compared with other contagious behaviours?
options: It is the least contagious
It only spreads between animals
It is something people can easily control
It is the most contagious and hard to stop
questions.why: He calls it 'the most contagious behaviour' and 'something that you can't stop'.

questions.q: What were the researchers trying to find out?
options: Whether yawning gives our brains more oxygen
Whether our thinking plays a part in catching yawns
Whether children yawn more often than adults do
Whether yawning makes people feel more tired later
questions.why: Drury says they wanted to see 'if there is a cognitive element' to the behaviour.

options: We catch yawns more from people we feel close to
We catch yawns more from strangers than from friends
Only people who are already tired catch yawns
Yawning is not really contagious between people
questions.why: The more you identify with the in-group, the more likely you are to copy their behaviour.

questions.q: Why does John Drury mention emotions and scratching?
options: To explain what causes yawning in the first place
To show they are more contagious than yawning is
As behaviours we judge before deciding to copy them
To describe the signs that someone is bored or tired
questions.why: He says we judge whether the person exhibiting any behaviour, like an emotion or scratching, is relevant.

questions.q: According to Rob, when are you less likely to yawn?
options: When a family member yawns
When you are watching TV
When a close friend yawns
When a stranger yawns
questions.why: Rob says you are less likely to yawn if a stranger yawns than if family or friends do.
